# Building the ITS Model

## Learning objectives

By the end of this chapter, you will be able to:

- Explain segmented regression.
- Construct and fit a basic ITS model.
- Interpret immediate level changes and changes in trend.
- Select an appropriate outcome distribution.
- Assess model assumptions and diagnostics.

## Introduction

Segmented regression is commonly used to estimate changes in outcome levels and trends following an intervention.


## 4.1 Explain Segmented Regression

Explain the principles of segmented regression and why it is used in interrupted time series analysis.

## 4.2 Construct and Fit a Basic ITS Model

Learn how to create the time variable, intervention indicator, and time-since-intervention variable, then fit a basic ITS model in R.

## 4.3 Interpret Immediate Level Changes and Changes in Trend

Understand how to interpret changes in outcome levels immediately after an intervention and changes in the subsequent trend.

## 4.4 Select an Appropriate Outcome Distribution

Learn when to consider linear regression, Poisson regression, or negative binomial regression based on the outcome and data structure.

## 4.5 Assess Model Assumptions and Diagnostics

Assess autocorrelation, residual patterns, seasonality, model fit, and other relevant assumptions.
